props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda permits piercing an eggshell, filling it with oil and setting it on the mouth of the lamp

R' Yehuda: once we kept Shabbat in the upper story of the house of Nitza in Lod; we filled an eggshell with oil, pierced it and set it on the mouth of the lamp, and R' Tarfon and the elders there said nothing to us
Avin of Tzippori dragged a bench in a marble-floored upper story before R' Yitzchak ben Elazar
R' Yitzchak ben Elazar to Avin: if I am silent to you as the colleagues were silent to R' Yehuda, harm will come of it
[the prohibition is] a decree on a marble upper story on account of an ordinary upper story
the head of the synagogue of Botzra dragged a bench before R' Yirmeya Rabba
R' Yirmeya Rabba: like whom -- R' Shimon? R' Shimon spoke of large ones, which cannot [be moved otherwise]; of small ones he did not say it
Ulla: the dispute [of R' Shimon and his disputant over dragging] is over small ones
Ulla: but over large ones, all agree it is permitted [to drag them]
R' Shimon: a person may drag a bed, a chair and a bench, provided he does not intend to make a furrow
Ulla: the baraita's bed is like its chair -- small
R' Yirmeya Rabba: the baraita's chair is like its bed -- large
clothing sellers [of kilayim] sell in their usual way, provided they do not intend [to be shielded] from the sun in the sun or from the rain in the rain; the modest hang them on a stick behind them
Rabba: here, where one could act like the modest, it is like small [benches]
Rabba: and when he does not intend, R' Shimon permits it ab initio -- the clothing-sellers mishnah is R' Shimon's
